topics.name: Contusions, tSAH & Diffuse Axonal Injury
topics.blurb: Traumatic SAH, contusion progression, TICH surgery, and diffuse axonal injury grading/imaging.

topics.blurb: Linear, depressed, basilar fractures, CSF fistula, pneumocephalus, growing fracture, frontal sinus.

topics.blurb: Gunshot and stab wounds: prognosis, debridement principles, vascular imaging, and infection prophylaxis.

topics.blurb: BTF thresholds, tiered ICP therapy, landmark trials, decompressive craniectomy, and brain death.

topics.name: Traumatic Cerebrovascular Injury
topics.blurb: BCVI screening/grading, dissection, traumatic aneurysm, carotid-cavernous fistula, venous sinus injury.

topics.name: Trauma Systems & Prognosis
topics.blurb: ATLS integration, damage control, intubated exam, coagulopathy reversal, prognostic models, abusive head trauma.

concepts.name: TBI epidemiology and mechanisms
concepts.blurb: TBI epidemiology: falls and motor-vehicle crashes lead; bimodal age peaks; leading cause of trauma death and disability.

concepts.name: Primary vs secondary brain injury
concepts.blurb: Distinguishing irreversible primary impact injury from preventable secondary insults (hypoxia, hypotension, raised ICP) that management targets.
acgme: Primary vs Secondary Brain Injury - Mechanisms and Prevention

concepts.name: GCS-based TBI severity
concepts.blurb: Stratifying TBI as mild (GCS 13-15), moderate (9-12), or severe (8 or less) by post-resuscitation GCS.
acgme: TBI Classification - Mild Moderate Severe (GCS) and Marshall or Rotterdam CT Score

concepts.name: GCS scoring pitfalls
concepts.blurb: GCS confounders: intubation, sedation, intoxication, aphasia; motor score and pupillary response carry the most prognostic weight.

concepts.name: Marshall CT classification
concepts.blurb: Marshall CT classification grades diffuse injury and mass lesions; predicts intracranial hypertension and outcome.
acgme: TBI Classification - Mild Moderate Severe (GCS) and Marshall or Rotterdam CT Score

concepts.name: Rotterdam CT score
concepts.blurb: Rotterdam score sums basal cistern status, midline shift, mass lesion, and IVH/SAH for graded mortality prediction.
acgme: TBI Classification - Mild Moderate Severe (GCS) and Marshall or Rotterdam CT Score

concepts.name: Coup-contrecoup injury
concepts.blurb: Coup injury lies under the impact site; contrecoup opposite from brain rebound, producing classic frontotemporal contusions.
acgme: Neuropathology of Trauma - Coup-Contrecoup Herniation DAI Histology

concepts.name: Post-traumatic cerebral edema
concepts.blurb: Traumatic cytotoxic and vasogenic edema drives delayed ICP rise, typically peaking 48-96 hours after injury.

concepts.name: Traumatic herniation syndromes
concepts.blurb: Recognizing uncal, central, subfalcine, and tonsillar herniation from traumatic mass effect and acting emergently.
acgme: Transtentorial Uncal and Tonsillar Herniation - Recognition and Management

concepts.name: Concussion definition
concepts.blurb: Concussion is transient neurologic dysfunction from biomechanical force, usually with normal CT; a functional, not structural, injury.
acgme: Mild TBI and Concussion - Diagnosis Return-to-Play and CTE Considerations

concepts.name: Sideline concussion assessment
concepts.blurb: Sideline tools (e.g. SCAT) evaluate symptoms, cognition, and balance; no single test confirms concussion.

concepts.name: Graded return-to-play
concepts.blurb: Stepwise, symptom-limited return-to-play progression with no same-day return after a diagnosed concussion.
acgme: Mild TBI and Concussion - Diagnosis Return-to-Play and CTE Considerations

concepts.name: Return-to-learn protocol
concepts.blurb: Cognitive rest followed by graded academic reintegration, completed before full return-to-play in students.

concepts.name: Second impact syndrome
concepts.blurb: Catastrophic diffuse cerebral swelling from a repeat impact before recovery; rare but often fatal in young athletes.
acgme: Mild TBI and Concussion - Diagnosis Return-to-Play and CTE Considerations

concepts.name: Post-concussive syndrome
concepts.blurb: Persistent headache, dizziness, and cognitive or mood symptoms lasting weeks to months after mild TBI.

concepts.name: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy
concepts.blurb: CTE is perivascular tau deposition from repetitive head impacts, currently diagnosed only at autopsy.
acgme: Neuropathology of Degenerative Diseases - Alzheimer Parkinson ALS CTE

concepts.name: Mild TBI on anticoagulation
concepts.blurb: Anticoagulated or antiplatelet patients with mild TBI warrant CT and observation given delayed hemorrhage risk.

concepts.name: Non-contrast CT first-line
concepts.blurb: Non-contrast head CT is first-line for acute TBI, detecting hemorrhage, mass effect, fracture, and herniation.
acgme: Emergency CT Head Interpretation in TBI (Blood Herniation Midline Shift)

concepts.name: Canadian CT Head Rule
concepts.blurb: Canadian CT Head Rule identifies minor head injury patients needing CT via high- and medium-risk criteria.
acgme: Emergency CT Head Interpretation in TBI (Blood Herniation Midline Shift)

concepts.name: New Orleans Criteria
concepts.blurb: New Orleans Criteria guide CT in minor head injury with GCS 15; more sensitive but less specific than CCHR.

concepts.name: Midline shift measurement
concepts.blurb: Quantifying midline shift at the septum pellucidum; greater than 5 mm signals significant mass effect.

concepts.name: Repeat CT for progression
concepts.blurb: Repeat CT for neurologic decline or to track hemorrhagic progression of contusions and subdural collections.

concepts.name: CTA for vascular injury
concepts.blurb: CT angiography screens for blunt cerebrovascular injury and traumatic vascular lesions along high-risk trajectories.

concepts.name: MRI in TBI
concepts.blurb: MRI with SWI/GRE and DWI outperforms CT for diffuse axonal injury, brainstem, and nonhemorrhagic lesions.

concepts.name: Epidural hematoma pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Epidural hematoma collects between skull and dura, usually arterial and biconvex, often from a temporal bone fracture.
acgme: Epidural Hematoma - CT Diagnosis Temporal Artery Bleeding Emergent Craniotomy

concepts.name: Middle meningeal artery anatomy
concepts.blurb: Middle meningeal artery arises from maxillary artery via foramen spinosum and tears with pterional or temporal fractures.
acgme: Epidural Hematoma - CT Diagnosis Temporal Artery Bleeding Emergent Craniotomy

concepts.name: Lucid interval
concepts.blurb: Classic lucid interval: brief recovery of consciousness followed by deterioration as an arterial epidural hematoma expands.

concepts.name: Epidural hematoma CT findings
concepts.blurb: Biconvex (lentiform) hyperdensity that does not cross sutures but may cross midline and dural attachments.

concepts.name: EDH surgical indications
concepts.blurb: Bullock criteria: evacuate epidural hematoma greater than 30 cubic centimeters regardless of GCS, or with neurologic decline.
acgme: Epidural Hematoma - CT Diagnosis Temporal Artery Bleeding Emergent Craniotomy

concepts.name: EDH craniotomy and tack-up
concepts.blurb: Craniotomy for epidural evacuation with dural tack-up sutures to obliterate the epidural space and stop bleeding.

concepts.name: EDH outcome
concepts.blurb: Epidural hematoma outcome is excellent when evacuated before herniation; prognosis hinges on pre-operative neurologic status.

concepts.name: Venous and posterior fossa EDH
concepts.blurb: Venous epidural hematomas from sinus disruption (posterior fossa/vertex) progress slowly; selected small cases managed nonoperatively.

concepts.name: Acute SDH pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Acute subdural hematoma arises from torn bridging veins or cortical laceration; crescentic blood in the subdural space.
acgme: Acute Subdural Hematoma - Indications for Emergent Craniotomy

concepts.name: Crescentic SDH on CT
concepts.blurb: Crescentic (concave) hyperdensity that crosses sutures but not midline, spanning the convexity of a hemisphere.

concepts.name: Acute SDH presentation
concepts.blurb: Acute subdural hematoma presents with depressed consciousness and reflects worse underlying brain injury than epidural hematoma.

concepts.name: Acute SDH surgical indications
concepts.blurb: Bullock criteria: evacuate acute SDH if thickness exceeds 10 mm or midline shift exceeds 5 mm regardless of GCS.
acgme: Acute Subdural Hematoma - Indications for Emergent Craniotomy

concepts.name: Craniotomy vs craniectomy for ASDH
concepts.blurb: Large craniotomy versus primary decompressive craniectomy for acute SDH with brain swelling; RESCUE-ASDH informs the choice.

concepts.name: SDH in elderly/anticoagulated
concepts.blurb: Elderly or anticoagulated patients need urgent reversal and lower thresholds; atrophy permits large hematomas before symptoms.

concepts.name: Chronic SDH pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Chronic SDH is a liquefied collection with vascular neomembranes prone to recurrent microbleeds in atrophic elderly brains.
acgme: Chronic Subdural Hematoma - Burr Hole Drainage and Recurrence Management

concepts.name: Chronic SDH presentation
concepts.blurb: Chronic SDH presents insidiously with headache, gait disturbance, confusion, or focal deficit weeks after minor trauma.

concepts.name: Chronic SDH imaging
concepts.blurb: Chronic SDH appears hypodense or isodense; mixed density signals acute-on-chronic rebleeding and internal membranes.

concepts.name: Burr hole vs craniotomy for CSDH
concepts.blurb: Burr-hole drainage is first-line for chronic SDH; craniotomy with membranectomy is reserved for organized or recurrent collections.
acgme: Chronic Subdural Hematoma - Burr Hole Drainage and Recurrence Management

concepts.name: Subdural drain after evacuation
concepts.blurb: Placing a subdural drain after evacuation reduces chronic SDH recurrence (Santarius RCT; TOSCAN supports drainage).
acgme: Chronic Subdural Hematoma - Burr Hole Drainage and Recurrence Management

concepts.name: MMA embolization for CSDH
concepts.blurb: Middle meningeal artery embolization reduces chronic SDH recurrence as a surgical adjunct or standalone treatment.
acgme: Chronic Subdural Hematoma - Burr Hole Drainage and Recurrence Management

concepts.name: Chronic SDH recurrence
concepts.blurb: Chronic SDH recurs in roughly 10-20%; risks include anticoagulation, bilateral collections, and incomplete brain reexpansion.
acgme: Chronic Subdural Hematoma - Burr Hole Drainage and Recurrence Management

concepts.name: Traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage
concepts.blurb: Traumatic SAH is convexity sulcal blood from cortical vessel injury, usually managed nonoperatively unlike aneurysmal SAH.
acgme: Traumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage and Cortical Contusions

concepts.name: Cortical contusion pathology
concepts.blurb: Cortical contusions are hemorrhagic bruising at frontal and temporal poles that may blossom over 24-72 hours.
acgme: Traumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage and Cortical Contusions

concepts.name: Hemorrhagic progression of contusion
concepts.blurb: Contusions blossom over hours; coagulopathy and hypotension worsen progression, mandating repeat CT for decline.

concepts.name: Traumatic intracerebral hematoma
concepts.blurb: Traumatic intracerebral hematoma is a coalesced deep contusion producing focal mass effect.

concepts.name: Surgery for contusion/TICH
concepts.blurb: Evacuate contusion or TICH for progressive mass effect, neurologic decline, or refractory ICP per Bullock thresholds.
acgme: Traumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage and Cortical Contusions

concepts.name: Diffuse axonal injury pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: DAI is axonal shearing at gray-white junction, corpus callosum, and brainstem from rotational acceleration-deceleration forces.
acgme: Diffuse Axonal Injury - Pathophysiology MRI Susceptibility Imaging Prognosis

concepts.name: DAI grading
concepts.blurb: Adams DAI grades I-III by lesion depth: lobar gray-white, corpus callosum, then dorsolateral brainstem.
acgme: Diffuse Axonal Injury - Pathophysiology MRI Susceptibility Imaging Prognosis

concepts.name: DAI imaging
concepts.blurb: DAI is often CT-occult; SWI/GRE MRI reveals microhemorrhages and explains coma despite a normal CT.
acgme: Diffuse Axonal Injury - Pathophysiology MRI Susceptibility Imaging Prognosis

concepts.name: DAI prognosis
concepts.blurb: DAI prognosis tracks with grade and brainstem involvement; it is a common cause of persistent post-traumatic coma.

concepts.name: Linear skull fracture
concepts.blurb: Linear fractures are usually benign but flag underlying injury and raise epidural hematoma risk when crossing the MMA groove.
acgme: Skull Fractures - Linear Depressed Open - Management Principles

concepts.name: Depressed skull fracture
concepts.blurb: Elevate depressed fractures depressed beyond full skull thickness, or with deficit, dural breach, or cosmetic concern.
acgme: Skull Fractures - Linear Depressed Open - Management Principles

concepts.name: Open depressed fracture
concepts.blurb: Open (compound) depressed fractures need debridement, elevation, and antibiotics; dural laceration raises infection and seizure risk.
acgme: Skull Fractures - Linear Depressed Open - Management Principles

concepts.name: Basilar skull fracture signs
concepts.blurb: Basilar fracture signs: raccoon eyes, Battle sign, hemotympanum, CSF rhinorrhea or otorrhea, and cranial nerve palsies.
acgme: Skull Base Fractures - CSF Rhinorrhea Otorrhea Pneumocephalus

concepts.name: Traumatic CSF fistula
concepts.blurb: Confirm traumatic CSF leak with beta-2 transferrin; most resolve conservatively, while persistent leaks need repair.
acgme: Skull Base Fractures - CSF Rhinorrhea Otorrhea Pneumocephalus

concepts.name: CSF leak repair
concepts.blurb: Persistent CSF leaks escalate to lumbar drainage then endoscopic or open dural repair; prophylactic antibiotics remain debated.
acgme: Lumbar Drain Placement - Technique Indications and Complications

concepts.name: Pneumocephalus
concepts.blurb: Pneumocephalus is intracranial air from fracture or surgery that usually resorbs spontaneously.
acgme: Skull Base Fractures - CSF Rhinorrhea Otorrhea Pneumocephalus

concepts.name: Tension pneumocephalus
concepts.blurb: Tension pneumocephalus is ball-valve air under pressure (Mount Fuji sign) requiring emergent decompression.

concepts.name: Growing skull fracture
concepts.blurb: Growing skull fracture (leptomeningeal cyst) is a pediatric dural tear with progressive diastasis; cross-references pediatric trauma.

concepts.name: Frontal sinus fracture
concepts.blurb: Posterior table or duct involvement guides cranialization versus observation; risks include CSF leak and mucocele.
acgme: Complex Craniofacial Trauma - Frontal Sinus Orbit Skull Base Reconstruction

concepts.name: Ballistic injury pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Penetrating ballistic injury creates a permanent tract plus temporary cavitation; transferred energy determines tissue damage.
acgme: Penetrating Brain Injury - Gunshot Wounds - Surgical Management

concepts.name: Gunshot prognostic factors
concepts.blurb: Poor GSW prognosis: low GCS, fixed pupils, and bihemispheric, multilobar, or transventricular trajectory predict high mortality.
acgme: Penetrating Brain Injury - Gunshot Wounds - Surgical Management

concepts.name: Gunshot wound management
concepts.blurb: Debride accessible necrotic tissue and hematoma with watertight dural closure; aggressive deep fragment retrieval is unnecessary.
acgme: Penetrating Brain Injury - Gunshot Wounds - Surgical Management

concepts.name: Retained fragments
concepts.blurb: Retained bone or metal fragments are not routinely chased; removal is balanced against injuring eloquent tissue.

concepts.name: Stab wounds and impaled objects
concepts.blurb: Image stab wounds and impaled objects before removal; extract in the operating room with vascular control prepared.

concepts.name: Vascular imaging in penetrating injury
concepts.blurb: Trajectories near vessels or skull base mandate CTA or angiography to detect traumatic aneurysm or fistula.

concepts.name: Penetrating injury infection prophylaxis
concepts.blurb: Penetrating injury needs broad-spectrum antibiotics and tetanus; CSF leak and retained fragments raise abscess risk.

concepts.name: Post-penetrating seizure risk
concepts.blurb: Penetrating brain injury carries high post-traumatic seizure risk, supporting prophylactic antiepileptic therapy.

concepts.name: BTF ICP and CPP thresholds
concepts.blurb: Brain Trauma Foundation guidelines treat ICP above 22 mmHg and maintain cerebral perfusion pressure of 60-70 mmHg.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: CPP targets
concepts.blurb: Target cerebral perfusion pressure 60-70 mmHg, avoiding below 50 (ischemia) and aggressive above 70 (ARDS risk).
acgme: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure - CPP MAP - ICP Targets and Optimization

concepts.name: ICP monitor indications
concepts.blurb: BTF: monitor ICP in salvageable severe TBI (GCS 3-8) with abnormal CT, or normal CT plus risk factors.
acgme: ICP Monitoring - Parenchymal Monitor Placement and Interpretation

concepts.name: EVD vs parenchymal monitor
concepts.blurb: EVD both measures and treats ICP via CSF drainage; a parenchymal bolt only monitors but drifts less.
acgme: ICP Monitoring - Parenchymal Monitor Placement and Interpretation

concepts.name: Tiered ICP therapy
concepts.blurb: Tiered ICP protocol escalates from sedation and CSF drainage to osmotherapy, then hyperventilation, barbiturates, and surgery.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Mannitol vs hypertonic saline
concepts.blurb: For raised ICP, hypertonic saline is preferred in hypotension while mannitol induces diuresis and can drop preload.
acgme: Osmotherapy - Mannitol vs Hypertonic Saline - Mechanisms and Targets

concepts.name: Hyperventilation for ICP
concepts.blurb: Hyperventilation lowers ICP via vasoconstriction but only as a temporizing bridge; prolonged use risks ischemia.

concepts.name: Sedation and analgesia in TBI
concepts.blurb: Sedation and analgesia lower cerebral metabolism and ICP; watch for propofol infusion syndrome and hypotension.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Barbiturate coma
concepts.blurb: Pentobarbital coma titrated to burst suppression treats refractory ICP; it causes hypotension and immunosuppression.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Therapeutic hypothermia (EUROTHERM)
concepts.blurb: EUROTHERM showed prophylactic therapeutic hypothermia for ICP control worsened outcomes; it is not routinely recommended.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Decompressive craniectomy
concepts.blurb: Decompressive craniectomy relieves refractory intracranial hypertension by removing a large bone flap with expansile duraplasty.
acgme: Decompressive Craniectomy with Duraplasty - Technique and Indications (DECRA)

concepts.name: DECRA vs RESCUEicp
concepts.blurb: Early craniectomy for diffuse injury (DECRA) worsened outcomes; last-tier RESCUEicp cut mortality with more dependent survivors.
acgme: Decompressive Craniectomy with Duraplasty - Technique and Indications (DECRA)

concepts.name: Cranioplasty timing and complications
concepts.blurb: Cranioplasty restores the bone flap after craniectomy; timing balances infection and resorption against syndrome of the trephined.
acgme: Cranioplasty - Autologous Bone Flap Replacement and Staged Protocol

concepts.name: Post-traumatic seizure prophylaxis
concepts.blurb: Seven days of phenytoin or levetiracetam reduces early post-traumatic seizures but not late epilepsy (Temkin).
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Steroids harmful (CRASH)
concepts.blurb: The CRASH trial showed corticosteroids increase mortality in TBI, making them contraindicated.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Brain tissue oxygen (PbtO2)
concepts.blurb: Brain tissue oxygen monitoring guides therapy; BOOST trials test whether oxygen-directed care improves severe-TBI outcomes.
acgme: Cerebral Metabolism Monitoring - Jugular Bulb O2 Brain PO2 (Licox) Microdialysis

concepts.name: BEST:TRIP interpretation
concepts.blurb: BEST:TRIP found ICP-monitor-guided care not superior to imaging/exam-based protocol; it does not argue against monitoring.

concepts.name: Trauma-induced coagulopathy
concepts.blurb: Trauma-induced coagulopathy worsens intracranial hemorrhage; correct INR and platelets and reverse anticoagulants urgently.
acgme: Coagulopathy Reversal in Neurosurgery - Warfarin NOAC Antiplatelet Reversal

concepts.name: Tranexamic acid (CRASH-3)
concepts.blurb: CRASH-3 showed early tranexamic acid within 3 hours reduces head-injury death in mild-to-moderate TBI.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Brain death determination
concepts.blurb: Brain death requires irreversible coma, absent brainstem reflexes, and a positive apnea test; confirmatory tests when exam is confounded.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: BCVI screening
concepts.blurb: Blunt cerebrovascular injury screening (Denver/Memphis criteria) with CTA prevents missed stroke from carotid/vertebral injury.
acgme: Traumatic Carotid and Vertebral Artery Dissection - Screening and Management

concepts.name: Traumatic arterial dissection
concepts.blurb: Traumatic carotid or vertebral dissection creates an intimal tear with thromboembolism; antithrombotics reduce stroke risk.
acgme: Traumatic Carotid and Vertebral Artery Dissection - Screening and Management

concepts.name: Biffl/Denver BCVI grading
concepts.blurb: Biffl (Denver) grades I-V stratify blunt cerebrovascular injury and guide antithrombotic versus endovascular management.

concepts.name: Traumatic aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Traumatic pseudoaneurysm from arterial wall disruption carries delayed rupture risk near skull base or penetrating tracts.

concepts.name: Carotid-cavernous fistula
concepts.blurb: Post-traumatic carotid-cavernous fistula causes pulsatile proptosis, chemosis, bruit, and ophthalmoplegia; treated endovascularly.
acgme: Traumatic Carotid and Vertebral Artery Dissection - Screening and Management

concepts.name: Traumatic venous sinus injury
concepts.blurb: Fractures crossing dural venous sinuses risk laceration or thrombosis; management weighs repair against controlled observation.
acgme: Venous Sinus Laceration Repair During Trauma Surgery

concepts.name: BCVI management
concepts.blurb: Most blunt cerebrovascular injuries are treated with antithrombotics; stenting or occlusion targets pseudoaneurysm or progression.
acgme: Traumatic Carotid and Vertebral Artery Dissection - Screening and Management

concepts.name: ATLS integration in TBI
concepts.blurb: ATLS primary survey precedes neurosurgical care; hypoxia and hypotension are major secondary insults to prevent.
acgme: Polytrauma Triage - ATLS Integration with Neurosurgical Decision-Making

concepts.name: Polytrauma prioritization
concepts.blurb: Polytrauma prioritization controls hemorrhage first, then sequences and times cranial surgery against other life-threats.

concepts.name: Damage-control neurosurgery
concepts.blurb: Damage-control neurosurgery performs rapid decompression and hemostasis, deferring definitive repair in the unstable polytrauma patient.

concepts.name: Hypotension and hypoxia insults
concepts.blurb: Even single episodes of hypotension or hypoxia after TBI markedly worsen outcome, driving aggressive resuscitation targets.

concepts.name: Neuro exam in intubated patient
concepts.blurb: Examine the intubated, sedated patient with pupils, brainstem reflexes, and motor response, using sedation holds when safe.

concepts.name: Coagulopathy reversal in trauma
concepts.blurb: Reverse warfarin with PCC and vitamin K, NOACs with idarucizumab or andexanet, and address antiplatelets before intervention.
acgme: Coagulopathy Reversal in Neurosurgery - Warfarin NOAC Antiplatelet Reversal

concepts.name: IMPACT and CRASH models
concepts.blurb: IMPACT and CRASH prognostic models estimate severe-TBI outcome from age, GCS, pupils, CT, and secondary insults.
acgme: Prognostication in Severe TBI - IMPACT Model Withdrawal of Care Discussions

concepts.name: Prognostication pitfalls
concepts.blurb: Avoid early self-fulfilling withdrawal of care; severe-TBI outcomes can improve over months of recovery.
acgme: Prognostication in Severe TBI - IMPACT Model Withdrawal of Care Discussions

concepts.name: Abusive head trauma
concepts.blurb: Abusive head trauma shows subdural hematomas and retinal hemorrhages in infants; mandates reporting and cross-references pediatric trauma.
acgme: Abusive Head Trauma (Shaken Baby Syndrome) - Diagnosis and Legal Considerations

concepts.name: EVD via Kocher point
concepts.blurb: Emergent EVD via Kocher point treats traumatic hydrocephalus and ICP; complications include hemorrhage, malposition, and infection.
acgme: Ventriculostomy (EVD) Placement - Kocher Point Technique and Complications

concepts.name: Extra-axial hemorrhage CT differentiation
concepts.blurb: Distinguish epidural (biconvex), subdural (crescentic), and subarachnoid (sulcal) blood on noncontrast head CT.
